_comment: TWELVE fixed planet layouts, not five. A generation dispatches 8 DISTINCT keys (plan.md 7.1) so the demo grid shows eight visibly different worlds while every one stays exactly replayable. Layouts must differ in CHARACTER, not just coordinates - eight near-identical fields teach the policy nothing and look like a bug on screen.

dispatch.rule: sample 8 distinct layout_ids from `train` without replacement each generation
dispatch.note: 8 of the 10 training layouts per generation, so the batch rotates and no layout is memorised.

layout_intent.0: planet straddling the direct craft-to-portal path - forces a detour
layout_intent.1: mass concentration off to one side - tempts a slingshot
layout_intent.2: two small planets flanking the approach corridor - narrow gate
layout_intent.3: one heavy planet close to the star - steep combined well
layout_intent.4: three light planets scattered wide - weak field, mostly navigation
layout_intent.5: planet directly behind the portal - overshoot is punished hard
layout_intent.6: two planets in line, corridor between them - threading required
layout_intent.7: heavy planet on the far side - a slingshot is the efficient route
layout_intent.8: near-empty field - tests that the policy does not over-avoid
layout_intent.9: dense cluster on one flank - large detour or a careful pass
layout_intent.10: HELD OUT - asymmetric pair, unseen geometry
layout_intent.11: HELD OUT - heavy planet adjacent to the portal, tests the A7 speed gate under pull
